title: Admissible transition labels
statement: Let $w$ be a Boolean, let $v_c$ be an optional Boolean, and let $\ell$ be a transition label with optional value-tape and mark-tape writes, a work-head move, an optional emitted Boolean, and an optional next state. The label is admissible precisely when it makes no value-tape write and either makes no mark-tape write or writes a marked true value while $v_c$ is present. If there is no next state, an emitted Boolean must be present; if the next state is a first-read state carrying phase $\phi'$, no Boolean is emitted, $\mathrm{main}(\phi')$ holds, the head is stationary or moves positively with $v_c$ present, and if $\mathrm{walk}(\phi')$ is false then $w$ is false and the head is stationary. If the next state is a value-rewind state carrying a phase $\phi'$, no Boolean is emitted, $\mathrm{main}(\phi')$ holds, $\mathrm{walk}(\phi')$ is false, the head moves negatively, and $v_c$ is present; if the next state is an append state, no Boolean is emitted, the head is stationary, no mark-tape write is made, and $w$ is false. Every other next state is inadmissible.
hypotheses_covered: Mark-tape write is absent or writes true while $v_c$ is present
Output is present when there is no next state
All other next states are inadmissible
caveat: The snippet does not define the phase predicates $\mathrm{main}$ and $\mathrm{walk}$, so their meanings cannot be stated from the supplied material.
